original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Whether a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 can act irreducibly on a joint image of dimension 5 or more.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package instead answers the open question of #6962: one explicit complete no-edge pattern-dimension-4 pool with irreducible joint image at least 5, or an upper bound under those hypotheses. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921 and #6962.
bottleneck_link: Side result. Irreducible joint image 5 occurs in pattern dimension 4, so a later word argument cannot quote an irreducible ceiling of 4 there. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet, and the selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once one explicit complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 is proved to act irreducibly on a five-dimensional joint image at every width at least 5. Do not classify all pattern-dimension-4 pools or claim an upper bound.
evidence: PROOF.md exhibits five rank-one idempotents whose patterns span a four-dimensional no-edge space, reconstructs every lift among the fifteen nonzero patterns, and shows that the hit digraph is strongly connected, so the action on the five-dimensional joint image is irreducible. verify.py repeats the pattern census, the width-5 through width-7 pool scan, the F2^5 subspace lattice, and the reducible normal-form control.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the pool search, the case analysis, and the package verifier. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 act irreducibly on a joint image of dimension 6 or more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The five-projector pool shows that irreducible dimension 5 occurs, so an upper bound must be at least 5, but it does not decide whether 5 is the maximum.
open_questions.first_step: Either give one explicit complete no-edge pattern-dimension-4 pool with joint-image dimension at least 6 and a written invariant-subspace check, or prove that 5 is an upper bound under these same hypotheses.
open_questions.blocked_by: No support reduction in this package bounds the search, and a search that finds no example would not be a proof.
